name: digitalcorpora unsigned-S3 range-fetch technique
purpose: Discover and range-read corpus files/metadata on digitalcorpora's public S3 bucket without an AWS account, for GAP-100 sampling.
verification_evidence: GET https://digitalcorpora.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=... returns S3 ListObjectsV2 XML (200 OK) with no credentials; range-fetching the first 2,000,000 bytes of corpora/files/CC-MAIN-2021-31-PDF-UNTRUNCATED/metadata/cc-provenance-20230303.csv.gz and decompressing via zlib.decompressobj(16+zlib.MAX_WBITS) yielded 12,946 usable CSV rows in 1.33s (OBS-0800); HEAD + central-directory read of a 1.66GB zip member (zipfiles/0000-0999/0001.zip) via HTTP range requests succeeded in 1.19s with 1 request, listing 1000 entries.
rationale: Confirmed fast and reliable; this is the working backbone for GAP-100's stratified sampler design, independent of the (currently blocked) CDX server and of data.commoncrawl.org's own reachability for the metadata half of the pipeline.
alternatives: aws s3 --no-sign-request (not installed; unnecessary given the raw XML API works)

name: data.commoncrawl.org WARC range-fetch access
purpose: Fetch the actual crawled-page bytes (WARC payload) paired against each truncation-pair metadata row (GAP-100).
verification_evidence: A direct Range GET to a data.commoncrawl.org WARC segment (the exact access pattern OBS-0201 used successfully in an earlier session) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden today (2026-09-27), reproduced with tries=1 (no retry). $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status shows no relay failure for this host at the time of the 403s, meaning the TLS/TCP tunnel succeeded and the 403 came from Common Crawl's own origin. Two full sampler runs (30 pairs across zips 0001/0002; a reduced 6-pair single-zip run) both timed out (600s, 170s) with zero completed rows before this was diagnosed (see OBS-0800). Chair re-check the same day: the first ranged GET on warc.paths.gz returned 206; after four more requests within about a minute, ranged GETs on both the paths file and a WARC segment returned 403 (a 919-byte Common Crawl HTML page), with or without a custom User-Agent, while a HEAD on the WARC returned 200. That pattern fits rate limiting after a burst, not a permanent block. commoncrawl.s3.amazonaws.com also returned 403 without credentials.
rationale: This blocks GAP-100's plan to scale the natural-pairs sampler beyond what OBS-0201 already captured historically. Not probed further (no User-Agent variation tried) per the standing 'don't work around a block' instruction. Needs the chair's attention: it affects not just new sampling but also *reproducibility* of OBS-0201 itself on a future date. Chair: treat as throttling until shown otherwise. The WP-3.7 sampler must pace itself (seconds between requests, back off on 403) and the Stage 4 verifier re-tests at a slow rate. Authenticated S3 access with a free AWS account is a lead from memory, unverified; it goes to the access gate only if the slow re-test also fails.
alternatives: slow, paced range reads with backoff (re-test in Stage 4)
authenticated S3 access to the commoncrawl bucket (unverified lead)

verification_evidence: www.ohchr.org returns HTTP 403 from this container (not retried further). unicode.org/udhr/index.html loads (200) but states hosting has moved to OHCHR/UN and every former data-file path 404s: /udhr/d/udhr_eng.txt, /udhr/assemblies/udhr_txt.zip, /udhr/unaccented/udhr_eng.txt all 404 (SRC-0801). name: radamsa
purpose: Generic mutation-based fuzzer/fault-injector for DMG-009 damage templates.
verification_evidence: git clone --depth 1 https://gitlab.com/akihe/radamsa.git (684KB) && make -j2 -> bin/radamsa, version string 'Radamsa 0.8a'. radamsa -s 1 sample_orig.pdf > mutated_radamsa.pdf: orig len 411513, mutated len 411596, 389954 bytes differing over the shared prefix. alternatives: zzuf (TOOL-422, simpler bit-flip-style mutation)

name: Provenance/test-spec format candidates: NIST CFTT, DFXML, CASE/UCO
purpose: Pick a per-repair provenance record format (GAP-010) and assess NIST CFTT-style test-spec templates (GAP-050).
license: CC0-1.0 OR LGPL-3.0-only (dfxml_python); Apache-2.0 (CASE and UCO)
verification_evidence: dfxml_python: not on PyPI under 'dfxml'/'dfxml-python' (both 404 from PyPI's JSON API); installed via `pip install git+https://github.com/dfxml-working-group/dfxml_python.git` as package 'dfxml' v1.0.2. Round-trip check: built a FileObject with filename/filesize/sha256 for sample_orig.pdf, serialized via DFXMLObject.to_dfxml(), and confirmed the correct sha256 hex digest is present in the 461-byte XML output (OBS-0801). CASE/UCO: LICENSE files fetched (both Apache-2.0), git tags confirmed up to 1.5.0 for both (casework/CASE and ucoProject/UCO). NIST CFTT: not independently re-checked this session (a prior, pre-compaction search already found no PDF/document-repair test-spec category there, corroborating GAP-050 -- not re-verified with a fresh URL fetch this session, so treat that specific claim as memory-sourced/Assess-level, distinct from this entry's own Trial verdict on DFXML/CASE/UCO).
rationale: Recommendation: use DFXML for the low-level, per-file record (hash, size, byte ranges touched by a repair) -- it is small, US-government-licensed (no clean-room concern), and hands-on confirmed working -- and layer CASE/UCO's higher-level ontology on top for the *event* semantics of a repair action (what tool, what action, what evidence), since CASE/UCO is designed exactly for chaining 'action -> evidence -> provenance' records and is Apache-2.0 (no clean-room concern either). NIST CFTT's test-spec *template structure* (requirements, assertions, test cases) is worth reusing as a document template for the held-out suite's own spec, even though CFTT itself has no PDF-repair category to borrow content from.
alternatives: PREMIS (digital-preservation metadata standard, not checked this session)
